COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
26.04.2024 SPA No. 82 of 2024
Hon’ble Ritu Bahri, C.J.
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Amar Murti Shukla, learned counsel for the 
appellant. 
2. The appellant in the present case has worked 
from 1976 till 22.2.1998, i.e. for a period of almost 22 
years. Thereafter, the appellant remained absent from 
service for 15 years, and his services were brought to 
an end. However, after rendering 22 years of service, 
his services could not have been terminated. At best 
he could have been given minimum pension, because 
there were no allegations against him during the period 
he served. 
3. Notice of motion. 
4. Mr. P.C. Bisht, learned Additional Chief Standing 
Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand accepts notice on 
behalf of the respondent nos. 1 to 7 & 9. 
5. Counsel for the State shall file a better affidavit, 
explaining why punishment of termination has been 
awarded to the appellant, and what benefit has been 
given to him. 
6. List on 05.06.2024.
 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) (Ritu Bahri, C.J.)

Rahul
